Thanks for your enquiry. Your reference is {reference}.

We have passed it to {count, plural, =0 {our team, who will match it to operators manually} one {# operator} other {# operators}}. They will reply to you directly, usually within a day.

— Explore Tanzania

whenToGo.metaTitle: Where to go in {month} — East Africa safari conditions
whenToGo.metaDescription: Wildlife, weather, crowds and rainfall for {month} across 46 East African destinations. Best this month: {best}.
whenToGo.intro: Conditions across all {count} destinations we cover, ranked for {month}. Wildlife viewing first, then weather, with the quieter option leading where two places are equally good.
whenToGo.quietBody: Strong weather this month without the high-season crowds — usually the best value on the calendar.
whenToGo.tableNote: Ratings are out of five. Crowds invert: more bars means busier.
whenToGo.tableCaption: Wildlife, weather, crowd level, rainfall and temperature for each destination in {month}
whenToGo.disclaimer: Climate normals and typical patterns, not a forecast. East African rains have been arriving less predictably than these averages suggest — treat them as a guide to the shape of the year, not a promise about a given week.
whenToGo.hubMetaTitle: When to go on safari in East Africa
whenToGo.hubIntro: Every month has a case for it. The migration moves, the rains come and go, and the quiet months are often the best value. Pick a month to see conditions across all 46 destinations.
whenToGo.hubMetaDescription: Where to go each month across Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda — wildlife, weather, crowds and rainfall for all 46 destinations.

events.intro: Annual events across Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda, listed by the month they usually fall in. Most organisers confirm dates a few months ahead — where they have not, this page says so rather than guessing.
events.metaTitle: Events in East Africa — festivals, ceremonies and races by month
events.metaDescription: Annual festivals, ceremonies and sporting events across Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda, with the month each falls in and what to plan around.
events.disclaimer: Months are habitual rather than fixed, and several of these follow lunar or announced calendars that move year to year. Confirm with the organiser before booking travel around one.

hiddenGems.intro: Six destinations in East Africa carry almost all of the attention. These {count} are quieter, and every one of them is set against the famous place it could replace — with the reason it stays quiet stated plainly, because that reason is usually a flight, a road, or a shorter list of lodges.
hiddenGems.metaTitle: Hidden gems in East Africa — quieter alternatives to the famous parks
hiddenGems.metaDescription: Under-visited destinations in Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda, each set against the well-known place it could replace, and each with its trade-off stated.
hiddenGems.disclaimer: Quiet places are quiet for reasons that change: a new airstrip, a road resurfaced, a lodge that closes. Check access and opening with an operator before committing to one of these.
hiddenGems.alternativesIntro: {name} is on nearly every itinerary, which is both why it is good and why it is busy. These are the places travellers choose when they want the same thing with fewer vehicles — each with what it costs you to go there instead.

tripCost.intro: Build the trip you are considering and see the range, using published day rates and park fees for {count} destinations. Ranges rather than a figure, because where you sleep and how many of you there are move the total more than anything else.
tripCost.metaTitle: East Africa trip cost calculator — safari, gorilla and beach budgets
tripCost.metaDescription: Estimate what a trip through Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda or Rwanda costs. Published day rates and park fees by destination, with the government fee floor shown separately.
tripCost.allAdded: Every destination is already in your trip
tripCost.empty: Add a destination above to start. Most first safaris are two or three stops over seven to ten nights.

tripCost.floor: Of that, {amount} per person is government park fees. Every operator pays the same, so a quote below that floor is not a better deal — it is a different trip.
tripCost.missing: No published figures yet for {names}, so nothing has been added for those nights. The total below covers the rest.
tripCost.excludes: Excludes international flights, visas, travel insurance, tips and drinks. Domestic flights between parks are not included either — they are commonly US$200–400 a leg.
tripCost.getQuote: Get real quotes for this trip
tripCost.disclaimer: This is an estimate built from published day-rate bands and park fees, not a quote. Prices move with season, group size and availability, and park fees are revised annually. Use it to tell a reasonable quote from an unreasonable one, then get a real one.

about.metaDescription: What this site is, how the listings were built, who is behind it, and how it makes money. Including the numbers that are not flattering.
about.lede: A directory and a set of planning tools for East African travel, built on the idea that a traveller deciding where to spend several thousand dollars deserves numbers somebody actually checked.
about.howBody1: Most sites in this category start with whoever pays to be there, which produces a list of the companies with the biggest marketing budget rather than the ones running the best trips. We started from the other end: public sources — operator websites, tourism board registers, business listings — compiled into a directory that was useful before anybody paid for anything.
about.howBody2: That is where the {count} listings come from. Operators can claim theirs, correct it, add packages and answer enquiries. Paying moves them up in how enquiries are distributed. It does not let anybody buy a review, a rating, or a claim about their trips that is not true.
about.honestTitle: The part most directories leave out
about.honestClaimed: Of {total} listings, {claimed} have been claimed by the business they describe. The rest were compiled from public information and nobody at that company has confirmed a word of it. Details can be out of date and some of those businesses will have stopped trading. Check before you pay anyone.
about.honestVerified: Verification is a separate and much narrower thing: {verified} listing carries a verified badge, which means we confirmed the person claiming it controls the business domain or email. It has never meant we inspected a vehicle or met a guide, and it should not be read that way.
about.p1Body: Every cost figure carries the year it was checked. Park fees are stated separately from day rates, because that portion is set by a government and identical for every operator — so a quote below it is not a better deal, it is a different trip with something removed.
about.p2Title: Let anyone buy the appearance of quality
about.p2Body: A paid plan changes how many enquiries an operator receives and what they can publish. It cannot buy a rating, a review, a verified badge, or a discount claim measured against a price they invented.
about.p3Title: Guess when we do not know
about.p3Body: A festival with no announced dates says so instead of showing a plausible one. A destination with no published costs is named as missing from an estimate rather than quietly left out. An offer whose length nobody has confirmed does not get a number.
about.moneyBody: Operators pay for subscriptions that improve their placement and unlock features such as packages and offers. Travel guide pages carry advertising. Travellers pay nothing, there are no booking fees, and no commission is taken on any trip — we are not in the transaction at all.

contact.metaDescription: Report a wrong price, request a correction or takedown, make a data request, or tell us about a bug.
contact.lede: Most people who land here want one of two things that work better elsewhere on the site. Those are below. Everything else — a wrong price, a takedown, a data request, a bug — goes in the form.
contact.travellerBody: Describe what you are planning and we will match you with operators who run that kind of trip. They reply to you directly, usually within a day or two.
contact.operatorBody: Find your listing and claim it. If your email or website domain matches what we hold, you are verified immediately and can correct anything that is wrong.
contact.formBody: This reaches an admin inbox on this site. There is no automated reply, and no email goes out — somebody reads it.

topic.correction: Something on the site is wrong
topic.takedown: Remove a listing or a review

contact.messagePlaceholder: The day rate on the Ruaha page looks about $200 too high for 2026 — the park authority published new figures in March.
contact.messageHint: If you are reporting something wrong on a page, telling us which page and what is wrong saves a round trip.
contact.sentBody: It is in the admin inbox. If it needs a reply you will get one at the address you gave.
contact.privacyNote: We store your name, email and message so somebody can answer you, and the page you came from if you arrived from one. Nothing else. See the privacy page for what happens to it.

error.invalid: Please check the name and email address.
error.tooShort: Please write at least a couple of sentences — a message we cannot act on helps neither of us.
error.rateLimited: You have sent several messages recently. Give us a chance to read those first.
error.generic: That did not send. Please try again.

contact.directBody: Phone and WhatsApp are the quickest way to reach us, and are answered from Tanzania during East African business hours.

search.metaDescription: Search destinations, guides, things to do, events and operators across East Africa.
search.lede: Destinations, guides, things to do, events and operators — all of it, in one box.
search.label: Search
search.emptyBody: Try a place name, a park, or what you want to do — “Serengeti”, “gorilla trekking”, “whale shark”. Spelling variations of Swahili names are a common cause of this.

compare.metaDescription: Put two or three tour operators side by side: day rates, response times, coverage and verification.
compare.lede: Two or three at a time, on the rows that actually decide it. Every figure comes from the operator’s own listing, and a blank means they have not published one rather than that the answer is zero.
compare.caption: Operators compared across day rate, rating, response time, coverage, packages and founding year
compare.rowRateNote: Per person per day, as the operator states it
compare.rowRatingNote: From reviews on this site only
compare.rowResponseNote: Measured on enquiries sent through this site
compare.rowDestinationsNote: Places they have told us they operate in
compare.ratingValue: {rating} from {count, plural, one {# review} other {# reviews}}
compare.shareHint: This comparison is in the address bar — copy it to send to whoever you are travelling with.
compare.emptyBody: Pick two or three operators from the directory and they will appear here side by side.
compare.disclaimer: Day rates and founding years are supplied by operators and not independently audited. Ratings and reply times are measured from activity on this site, so an operator with few enquiries has little history behind those numbers.

billing.payIntro: Transfer {amount} to the account below, quoting the reference. Nothing is charged automatically and no card is involved.
billing.payAlreadyPaid: This payment has been confirmed and the plan is active.
billing.referenceHint: Put {reference} in the reference or narration field of the transfer. It is how we match your payment — without it we cannot tell your transfer from anyone else’s.
billing.next1: Make the transfer from your bank or mobile banking app.
billing.next2: Make sure {reference} appears in the reference field.
billing.next3: We check received payments against the bank statement. This is done by a person, so allow one working day.
billing.next4: Once matched, your plan activates for twelve months and you will see it on this page.
billing.tellUsWhatsApp: Tell us it is sent on WhatsApp — {phone}
billing.fraudWarning: The only account we ever ask you to pay is {account} at CRDB Bank, in the name shown above. If anyone gives you different details claiming to be us, it is not us. Check here first.
